401	For here too, the verse equates fulfilling his own needs with
402	"for it is good for him with you," said of the Hebrew servant.
403	So that here too, if he has only one chair
404	and his friend has no chair at all, the halachic ruling is that if he sits on it
405	and does not give it to his friend, he transgresses the positive commandment of "love your neighbor
406	as yourself," because he does not fulfill his friend's needs as he fulfills his own.
407	And if he does not sit on it, and also does not give it to his friend, this is wickedness, like the way of
408	Sodom.
409	Rather, he is obligated to give it to his friend to sit on, and he himself should sit on the ground or stand.
410	And it is understood that the same law applies to all the needs
411	that he has and his friend lacks. From here, go and learn whether this mitzvah
412	is within the realm of possibility to fulfill.
413	I am asking for a definitive answer.
414	Yes.
415	Yes.
416	Definitive.
417	Yes.
418	You can understand that, say...
419	That is, just as we, say, set ourselves aside for our children's needs,
420	there we often don't even think about it.
421	If my daughter comes to visit, for example, and there is only one chair,
422	I won't think twice at all.
423	It is clear.
424	Why?
425	Because with children there is natural love.
426	So that is clear, right?
427	If, say, the children are crying, and someone here has to
428	volunteer and not sleep, it will be me, without any doubt, because I was there and I am not a
429	woman.
430	So with our children things are simple, the sacrifice
431	and the willingness are natural.
432	Now the Torah comes and says, I ask you to take the model of
433	the children and apply it, to widen the circle.
434	A gentile servant is a bit, the conditions are a bit less good.
435	Doesn't the law of the convert, orphan and widow apply to him?
436	Convert, orphan and widow is something else.
